headline: This law requires the President to send Congress any nuclear agreement with Iran and limits sanctions relief during a review period.
what_it_does: The law requires the President to send Congress the text of any agreement with Iran on its nuclear program within five days, along with a State Department verification report and certifications about the deal. During a review period, the President cannot waive or ease statutory sanctions on Iran, and Congress can pass a resolution favoring or opposing the agreement, which controls whether relief may go forward. The President must also report Iranian compliance and breaches to Congress on set schedules.

who_it_affects.group: The President and executive branch agencies, including the State Department
who_it_affects.how: They must transmit agreements, prepare verification reports, and send Congress compliance reports and breach determinations on set deadlines.

who_it_affects.group: Iran's government and its nuclear program
who_it_affects.how: Any nuclear agreement with Iran is subject to congressional review, and statutory sanctions relief is limited during that review.

who_it_affects.group: Companies and banks doing business with Iran
who_it_affects.how: Statutory sanctions cannot be waived, eased, or lifted during the review period, so existing sanctions stay in force while Congress considers an agreement.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on May 22, 2015.
